newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones nominates seven board members.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones nominates seven board members.

text.p: Four members of Dow Jones & Co.'s board are leaving, the company -- whose internal struggle has made headlines recently -- announced late Monday.
The company, which publishes The Wall Street Journal and supplies business news and information, said Martha Robes was voluntarily retiring from the 15-member board after 16 years as a director.
The other three -- Donald Petersen, Warren Phillips and Richard Wood -- have reached the mandatory retirement age of 70, the New York-based company said.
Dow Jones said seven candidates had been nominated the board, four of them new.

Nominated to replace the outgoing board members were American Express Co. Chairman Harvey Golub, Leslie Hill, an American Airlines pilot and a member of the Bancroft family that holds a controlling interest in the company; Bankers Trust Chairman Frank Newman; and Pfizer Inc. Chairman William Steere.
Board members David Li, Jane MacElree and James Ottaway are seeking re-election to the board.
Dow Jones also said board members Carlos Salinas de Gortari, the former president of Mexico, and Carl Valenti, a company senior vice president, were not seeking re-election.

The board moves followed the announcement Friday by William Cox III, a member of the Bancroft family, that he was resigning as manager of Dow Jones' global stock indexes after 18 years with the company.
Cox and a cousin, Elisabeth Goth, have made headlines in recent weeks over their stated disappointment with the company's direction and the value of its stock.
Other family members, including Cox's father, William Cox Jr. -- who sits on the board -- have said they support Dow Jones management.
A Dow Jones spokesman Monday pointed out that neither the younger Cox nor Goth are board members.

Dow Jones' stock took a hit in late January after the company reported it would spend $650 million to expand and revitalise its Telerate financial information services unit. On the day of that announcement, the company's stock fell $4.50 to $36.375.
Dow Jones stock dropped 37.5 cents to $39.25 on the New York Stock Exchange Monday, before the announcement on the board was issued.
In addition to The Wall Street Journal, Dow Jones publishes Barron's magazine, Dow Jones news service and a variety of other financial information services.
